correctness.rationale: The original paper's monomer/dimer definition agrees with the frozen even-run parsing and legal moves. Each move changes one effective level by one or toggles just one dimer start. Dissolve source-only dimers, keep the common dimers (their endpoints already have target effective levels), adjust the remaining monomers monotonically, and insert target-only dimers. Target dimers are disjoint and each insertion is then legal, so the coordinate distance is attained. A list of moves and the label can be produced in O(kn) time; this does not count printing a full word per move. Threshold bits turn level differences into Hamming distance. For k=2r, consecutive bits inside a site block are a low test h<j<=r and a high test h>=j'>r, so cannot both be one. A dimer bit of one forces both neighbouring low tests to vanish. This permits precisely kn−1 positions, including at n=1. In an isometric hypercube encoding the metric cross-sums of two edges differ iff their bit directions coincide. The frozen witnesses use all kn−1 directions, hence require that many in any isometric encoding; every Fibonacci cube has its Hamming metric by dropping nonshared ones and then adding target ones. Distance one also proves that the image is induced.
residual_risks: The supplied finite BFS and label checks were inspected, not rerun; replay with python3 verify.py in the source directory. The proof does not assume those checks or settle arbitrary nonisometric embeddings.
